title: Victor Hugo's birth chart
metaDescription: Victor Hugo's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 7.2° Pisces. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Four of the ten placements whose signs are settled stand in Pisces — the Sun, Mercury, Venus and Pluto. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 7.2° Pisces — the first decan, 0°–10°, which the tradition sub-rules by Jupiter. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Pisces and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 25.1° Pisces, Venus was at 2.4° Pisces, Mars was at 0.7° Aquarius. Read together: a mind that absorbs before it argues; taste tuned to mood and undertow; drive that argues its way forward.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Closest first: Saturn to Pluto, an opposition with 1.5° of slack. An opposition puts two needs on opposite shores of the same water. Neither drowns; neither gets the whole beach. Behind it, Venus opposition Saturn at 1.5°, and the Sun conjunction Pluto at 1.8° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has two entries for this chart. Mercury in Pisces at 25.1° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Venus in Pisces at 2.4° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. None of these labels is a verdict on a person; they describe how a function is situated, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 5 water, 2 fire, 2 air, 1 earth by element and 6 mutable, 3 fixed, 1 cardinal by modality. A water emphasis keeps long books: little is forgotten, and nothing is felt only once. Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune were retrograde — the backward drift a body appears to make as the Earth overtakes it, read in the scheme as a function that reviews before it releases.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Sagittarius for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.9° between midnight and midnight. Fast enough that its degree is approximate, slow enough that its sign is not in doubt. At the noon reference it stands at 18.6°.
